Cleaning of the field survey data from the urban slums: women, children and households. The code is shown as written; it is not run when the site is built.

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rm(list = ls())
library(haven)
library(dplyr) 
library(rio) 
library(labelled)
library(ggplot2)
library(stargazer)
```
:::


Clears the workspace and loads the packages.

## Women's data: cleaning


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
W_SLUMS <- W_SLUMS %>%
  mutate(
    age           = ifelse(age == 0, NA, age),
    education     = ifelse(education > 16, NA, education))
summary(W_SLUMS$age)
W_SLUMS |> count(education)
```
:::


Age 0 and education above 16 are replaced with `NA`.

## Women's data: recoding


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
W_SLUMS <- W_SLUMS %>%
  mutate(
    # widow or separated = 1, others = 0
    widow_sep = ifelse(marital_status %in% c(3, 4), 1, 0),
    # age groups
    age_group = case_when(
      age < 18               ~ 1,    # below 18
      age >= 18 & age < 25   ~ 2,    # 18-24
      age >= 25 & age < 35   ~ 3,    # 25-34
      age >= 35 & age < 45   ~ 4,    # 35-44
      age >= 45 & age < 55   ~ 5,    # 45-54
      age >= 55 & age < 65   ~ 6,    # 55-64
      age >= 65              ~ 7     # 65+
    ),
    
    # factors
    slum_id      = as.factor(slum_id),
    joint_family = as.integer(joint_family == 1),
    fil_alive    = as.integer(fil_alive == 1),
    mil_alive    = as.integer(mil_alive == 1))

W_SLUMS <- W_SLUMS %>%
  mutate(
    edu_cat = case_when(
      education == 0                    ~ 1,   # Illiterate
      education >= 1  & education <= 5  ~ 2,   # Primary
      education >= 6  & education <= 8  ~ 3,   # Middle
      education >= 9  & education <= 10 ~ 4,   # Secondary
      education >= 11 & education <= 12 ~ 5,   # Higher Secondary
      education >= 13 & education <= 16 ~ 6    # Graduate & Above
    ))
```
:::


Widowed or separated indicator, age groups and education categories.

## Dummy variables


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# ── CREATE DUMMIES ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

W_SLUMS <- W_SLUMS %>%
  mutate(
    # education dummies
    edu_illiterate   = as.integer(edu_cat == 1),
    edu_primary      = as.integer(edu_cat == 2),
    edu_middle       = as.integer(edu_cat == 3),
    edu_secondary    = as.integer(edu_cat == 4),
    edu_higher_sec   = as.integer(edu_cat == 5),
    edu_graduate     = as.integer(edu_cat == 6),
    
    # age group dummies
    age_below_18     = as.integer(age_group == 1),
    age_18_24        = as.integer(age_group == 2),
    age_25_34        = as.integer(age_group == 3),
    age_35_44        = as.integer(age_group == 4),
    age_45_54        = as.integer(age_group == 5),
    age_55_64        = as.integer(age_group == 6),
    age_65plus           = as.integer(age_group == 7)
  )
```
:::


One 0/1 variable for each education and age category.

## Summary statistics


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
W_SLUMS %>%
  dplyr::select(
    # dependent variable
    currently_working,
    
    # independent variables — marital status
    widow_sep,
    
    # independent variables — family structure
    joint_family,
    
    # independent variables — age groups
    age_18_24,
    age_25_34,
    age_35_44,
    age_45_54,
    age_55_64,
    age_65plus,
    
    # control variables — education
    edu_illiterate,
    edu_primary,
    edu_middle,
    edu_secondary,
    edu_higher_sec,
    edu_graduate,
    
    # control variables — in-laws
    fil_alive,
    mil_alive
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  stargazer(
    type         = "text",
    title        = "Table 1: Summary Statistics — Determinants of Women's Employment in Urban Slums",
    summary.stat = c("n", "mean", "sd", "min", "max"),
    digits       = 2,
    covariate.labels = c(
      # dependent
      "Currently Working",
      
      # independent
      "Widowed/Separated",
      "Joint Family",
      
      # age groups
      "Age 18-24",
      "Age 25-34",
      "Age 35-44 (ref)",
      "Age 45-54",
      "Age 55-64",
      "Age 65+",
      
      # education
      "Illiterate (ref)",
      "Primary (1-5 years)",
      "Middle (6-8 years)",
      "Secondary (9-10 years)",
      "Higher Secondary (11-12 years)",
      "Graduate & Above",
      
      # controls
      "Father-in-law Alive",
      "Mother-in-law Alive"
    ))
```
:::


Summary table of the employment variables.

## Importing and merging


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
W_SLUMS <- rio::import("../data/ddd3/SLUMS/W_SLUMS.dta")





# data merging
# 1. 1:1:1 merge (merge by a unique identifier)
#new_data<- merge(data1, data2, by = c("identifiers"))

# 2. m:1 merge 
# new_data<- merge(data1, data2 by = c("identifiers"), all.x = TRUE)  : all.x = TRUE means that all rows from data1 will be kept, and only matching rows from data2 will be included.
# in this case we need to at place of data1  we need to keep many rows and at place of data2 we need to keep one row.
```
:::


Imports the women's data. The merge notes explain a one-to-one and a many-to-one merge.
